# Tom Bruno

> Tom Bruno is a Product and Ecosystem Leader in AI Ecosystems at Google, founder of Korext and creator of ACE, the open source African Context Engine. Born and raised in Kenya, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. He shapes strategy for how AI agents reach the web: what they can access, how they identify themselves, and what publishers and creators get in return.

Full name: Tom Bruno Makhanu.

## Work

- Now, Product and Ecosystem Leader in AI Ecosystems at Google: shaping strategy for how AI agents, platforms and publishers connect, covering access, identity, incentives and the protocols and standards that hold them together.
- Five years on Chrome: product and platform strategy for a browser used by billions of people, and Chrome Culture Ambassador during the team's shift to new ways of working.
- Earlier: Global Product Lead for AdSense, after starting full time in Large Customer Sales in Dublin. His Google career began with an internship at Google Kenya.
- Outside Google: Korext, ACE and Inclusive Skin AI are personal projects, separate from his work at Google. He invests in technology led founders in frontier markets with Black Angel Group, and advises Silicon Xchange, which connects Silicon Valley and Africa.

## Projects

- [ACE, the African Context Engine](https://tbrunoh.github.io/ace/): checked, local, citable knowledge for Africa on any phone (USSD, SMS/RCS, voice, WhatsApp and MCP). USSD, SMS and voice are the default, so every phone is reached; WhatsApp and RCS show the sources under every answer for people with a smartphone and data, and RCS adds suggested replies and falls back to SMS. RCS shipped in release 2.2.0b3 (26 November 2026), switched on country by country. It covers 34 countries in 32 languages, each offered in the countries that speak it, from English, Swahili and French to Hausa, isiZulu, Amharic and Tigrinya, and a safety rail answers emergencies with each country's verified numbers. Six decision services on dated public data (rain this week, official warnings, nearest health facility, market prices, a pregnancy companion and a crop problem check) cover every country wherever open data exists. Try it live at [ace.korext.com](https://ace.korext.com), a simulated phone for USSD, SMS, voice, WhatsApp and RCS that runs release 2.4.1 (27 November 2026); release 2.4.0b1 also added fire, drowning, stabbing and road accidents to the safety rail. Release 2.3 preview (2.3.0b1, 26 November 2026; 2.3.0b2, 27 November, with no default country) added 24 languages, among them Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Nigerian Pidgin, isiZulu, isiXhosa, Shona, Kinyarwanda, Lingala, Akan, Wolof and Tigrinya; 12 of them have a voice through Gemini TTS. ACE also tells a person when it does not read their language yet and names the languages it reads in their country, from letter profiles of 49 languages its callers speak but ACE does not. Release 2.2 preview (25 November 2026) added speech and translation: a language check on real speech text from the open WAXAL corpus, a voice line that speaks only languages with a known voice, Amharic and Somali through Gemini TTS, and optional Google Cloud speech providers. Release 2.1 (24 November 2026) added 21 countries and five languages. Open source under Apache 2.0, with context packs under CC BY 4.0; cite it as [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24565737](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24565737), which resolves to the latest version. The project page explains the problems ACE solves and answers common questions; the code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine).
- [ACE V2 services guide](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/services.md): the six services, their decision rules, coverage in all 34 countries and gaps.
- [ACE speech and translation guide](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/blob/main/docs/speech.md): what exists to hear, speak and translate each of ACE's 32 languages, the WAXAL language results and the voice line rule.
- [ACE V2 product design](https://github.com/tbrunoh/african-context-engine/tree/main/docs/v2): twelve decision services and a voice line on public weather, flood, soil and health data and open African speech models. Published 24 November 2026; six services shipped the same day as a preview.
- [Korext](https://korext.com): a governance runtime for AI generated code, with [seven open standards](https://oss.korext.com) that make AI written software traceable, licensable and accountable.
- [Inclusive Skin AI](https://github.com/tbrunoh#inclusive-skin-ai): skin analysis built for melanin-rich skin first, with a skin tone model on the Monk Skin Tone scale and an inference API; the code is open as a reference.

## Writing

- [AI for Africa has to work on the phone people already own](https://tbrunoh.github.io/writing/ai-for-africa-basic-phones/), 24 November 2026: almost a billion Africans live within reach of mobile internet and do not use it, so AI for Africa has to run on USSD, SMS and voice, with sources and safety built in.
- [Africa's farm data is open. The last mile to farmers is the work left to do](https://tbrunoh.github.io/writing/africa-farm-data-last-mile/), 24 November 2026: AI weather forecasts, rainfall records, soil maps and flood forecasts for Africa are free; turning them into decisions on a basic phone is the work left to do.
